  <section class="resource-section" id="r-routines" aria-labelledby="routines-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="routines-title">Frequent R routines</h2>
  <p>The cards below summarize what to use depending on the task. For details by package, use the package page.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Import</h3><p><code>readr::read_csv()</code>, <code>readxl::read_excel()</code>, <code>haven::read_sav()</code>. Always check with <code>glimpse()</code>, <code>names()</code> and <code>skimr::skim()</code>.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Select and filter</h3><p><code>dplyr::select()</code> keeps columns, <code>dplyr::filter()</code> keeps rows, <code>dplyr::arrange()</code> orders the table.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Create and summarize</h3><p><code>dplyr::mutate()</code> creates variables, <code>dplyr::group_by()</code> defines groups, <code>dplyr::summarise()</code> computes summaries.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Reshape</h3><p><code>tidyr::pivot_longer()</code> creates long data, <code>tidyr::pivot_wider()</code> widens a table, <code>tidyr::separate()</code> splits a column.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Clean text and categories</h3><p><code>stringr</code> helps detect, replace and extract text. <code>forcats</code> recodes and reorders factors.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Visualize</h3><p>Start with <code>ggplot()</code>, define variables with <code>aes()</code>, choose a <code>geom_*</code>, then polish titles, axes and facets.</p></article>
  </div>

  <section class="resource-section resource-split" id="quarto-github" aria-labelledby="workflow-title">
  <div>
  <h2 id="workflow-title">Minimal workflow</h2>
  <p>In STT-1100, reproducible work follows the same logic: open the right project, load packages, import data, write code in a Quarto document, render the document, then save important steps with GitHub when the module asks for it.</p>
  <div class="resource-actions">
  <a class="home-action home-action--primary" href="demarrage.html">Review the start page</a>
  <a class="home-action" href="autre_materiel/aide-memoire-rstudio-github.html">Clone with RStudio</a>
  </div>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-compact-list" aria-label="Work steps">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Project</h3><p>One folder, one Quarto file, data in the right place and explicit file names.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Report</h3><p>A clear title, readable code blocks and results interpreted in short sentences.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Version</h3><p>Small and understandable commits when the work is ready to save.</p></article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" id="before-submission" aria-labelledby="checklist-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <p class="eyebrow">Final check</p>
  <h2 id="checklist-title">Before submitting or pushing</h2>
  <p>This checklist avoids the most expensive mistakes: a missing file, an unexplained chart, a render failure or a vague commit.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="course-flow">
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">1</span>
  <h3>Render</h3>
  <p>The <code>.qmd</code> file must render without error on your machine, not only run a few chunks in the Console.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">2</span>
  <h3>Check data</h3>
  <p>Required files must be in the repository or accessible through the path written in the report.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">3</span>
  <h3>Interpret</h3>
  <p>Every important table or chart should have a sentence saying what is observed and what cannot be concluded.</p>
  </article>
  <article class="flow-card">
  <span class="flow-number">4</span>
  <h3>Save</h3>
  <p>If GitHub is required, make a commit with a precise message, then check that the remote repository contains the expected files.</p>
  </article>
  </div>
  </section>

  <section class="resource-section" id="troubleshooting" aria-labelledby="help-title">
  <div class="resource-section__header">
  <h2 id="help-title">Troubleshooting and help</h2>
  <p>Before asking for help, make the problem observable. This is also what makes the course AI useful.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="resource-hub-grid compact-hub">
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Read the error</h3><p>Copy the full message. Identify the function, object or file mentioned.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Reduce</h3><p>Rerun only the block that fails. Check that packages are loaded and data exist.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Compare</h3><p>Compare with a module example, the cheat sheet or the official documentation.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Phrase</h3><p>State the goal, minimal code, error message and expected result.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Check AI</h3><p>When an answer comes from AI, ask: <em>Which line should I test and what hypothesis does this test verify?</em> Then run the code and keep a trace of what was used.</p></article>
  <article class="resource-compact"><h3>Ask targeted help</h3><p>A good question includes context, the instruction followed, minimal code, the error and what you already tried. Example: <em>Here is my goal, minimal code, full message and what I already tried.</em></p></article>
  </div>
